constructs.name: Locating fractions on a number line
constructs.description: Place and read fraction positions between 0 and 1 (and beyond) on a number line.

levels.label: informal
misconceptions: Treats denominator as distance from 0
Ignores scale of the number line
student_language: It's somewhere in the middle
Closer to one I think

levels.label: partial
correct_behaviors: Places halves and fourths with prompting
misconceptions: Swaps numerator and denominator on the line
Uses only unit fractions as anchors
student_language: Is 3/4 past the half mark?
I put it near 1/2 but I'm not sure

levels.label: solid
correct_behaviors: Locates common fractions on a 0-1 line
misconceptions: Struggles with improper fractions on the same line
student_language: 3/4 is three jumps of 1/4 from 0

levels.label: generalized
correct_behaviors: Explains placement using equivalence and scale
student_language: It's the same point as 6/8

constructs.name: Comparing fractions with unlike denominators
constructs.description: Decide which of two fractions is greater when denominators differ.

levels.label: informal
misconceptions: Compares numerators only
Assumes larger denominator means larger fraction
student_language: 4 is bigger than 3 so 1/4 is bigger
I just look at the top number

levels.label: partial
misconceptions: Incorrect common denominator when attempting comparison
student_language: I think 2/3 is more than half
I'm not sure if I need the same bottom number

levels.label: solid
correct_behaviors: Compares using common denominators or equivalent fractions
misconceptions: Arithmetic slips after correct method chosen
student_language: I'll get the same denominator first

levels.label: generalized
student_language: These are equivalent so they're equal

constructs.name: Finding a common denominator
constructs.description: Identify and use a common denominator to add or subtract fractions.

levels.label: informal
misconceptions: Adds denominators directly
Uses product of denominators without adjusting numerators
student_language: Can't you just make the bottoms the same by adding them?
I don't know what LCD means

levels.label: partial
correct_behaviors: Finds a common denominator with hints (e.g. 6 for 2 and 3)
misconceptions: Finds LCD but forgets to scale numerators
Uses wrong multiple
student_language: Maybe 6 works?
I changed the bottom but forgot the top

levels.label: solid
correct_behaviors: Finds LCD and rewrites both fractions
misconceptions: Subtracts numerators correctly but slips on final simplification
student_language: 1/3 is 2/6 so now I can subtract

levels.label: generalized
correct_behaviors: Efficiently uses LCD across add/subtract contexts
student_language: The LCD is 12 because...

constructs.name: Adding and subtracting fractions
constructs.description: Combine fractions with like or unlike denominators in context.

levels.label: informal
misconceptions: Adds numerators and denominators straight across
Subtracts smaller from larger numerator only
student_language: You just add the tops and bottoms

levels.label: partial
misconceptions: Fails to convert unlike denominators before operating
student_language: I know you need the same denominator but I mess it up

levels.label: solid
misconceptions: Sign or arithmetic slip in multi-step problems
student_language: So 5/6 minus 2/6 is 3/6

levels.label: generalized
student_language: 3/6 simplifies to 1/2

constructs.name: Fraction-decimal-percent equivalence
constructs.description: Connect representations of rational numbers across fraction, decimal, and percent.

levels.label: informal
misconceptions: Treats percent as additive with fractions
student_language: 50% is like half I guess

levels.label: partial
correct_behaviors: Converts familiar fractions to decimals with support
misconceptions: Misplaces decimal point
Confuses 0.25 with 25%
student_language: 0.25 is 25 out of 100 maybe

levels.label: solid
student_language: 1/4 is 0.25 which is 25%

levels.label: generalized
student_language: They're all the same amount

constructs.name: Identifying ratio equivalence
constructs.description: Recognize when two ratios describe the same relationship.

levels.label: informal
misconceptions: Compares totals instead of part-to-part
Adds parts to get ratio
student_language: Isn't 2:3 the same as adding 2 and 3?

levels.label: partial
misconceptions: Doubles one part only when scaling
student_language: If I double one side do I double the other?

levels.label: solid
student_language: 4:6 is the same as 2:3

levels.label: generalized
student_language: The relationship stays the same

constructs.name: Unit rate and base ratio reasoning
constructs.description: Find per-one amounts and compare rates in context.

levels.label: informal
misconceptions: Divides in wrong order
Uses difference instead of rate
student_language: Which number do I divide by?
Is it just the bigger minus smaller?

levels.label: partial
correct_behaviors: Computes unit rate with a model or table
misconceptions: Unit rate correct but misapplies to comparison
student_language: Per one mile is... wait I confused miles and hours

levels.label: solid
student_language: $3 per pound means divide total by pounds

levels.label: generalized
student_language: The better deal has the lower cost per item
